P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Somalia is a dollarised economy: most prices are quoted in US dollars, and most domestic payments use mobile money and bank transfers in dollars. Diaspora remittances are large and flow largely through hawala and digital channels. No specific repatriation rule for individuals' service income was found; the Central Bank reportedly capped banks' dollar cash exports.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Single official-but-foreign source (trade.gov) captured; Central Bank of Somalia rules not captured on 2026-10-22.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: Use regulated channels (banks, licensed money transfer operators) - informal hawala routes carry AML risk.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: The federal government runs an online business registration and licensing system, launched in March 2022 with IFC/World Bank support. Registration takes about four days on average, in three steps. Sole-proprietor fees were not confirmed. Somaliland and other member states have separate systems.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: There is no VAT; a sales tax applies. Sources conflict on the rate. TaxAtlas gives about 5%, with no formal registration threshold. Trading Economics (citing the Ministry of Finance) records a fall to 5% in 2025 but shows 10% as its latest value. A formal VAT is being developed.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Data Protection Act 2023 (Law No. 005 of 2023), with a Somalia Data Protection Authority. Registration targets 'data controllers of major importance'. In May 2026 the Authority launched registration and oversight of controllers and processors, covering banks, fintechs, telecoms, NGOs and others, with six-monthly assessments.

sources.title: Unpacking the Somalia Data Protection Act of 2023
sources.quote: A data controller differs from a data controller of major importance in that the latter is either domiciled, resident or operating within Somalia.

sources.title: Somalia moves to tighten oversight of personal data handling (20 May 2026)
sources.quote: Mohamed Noor Olow, Director of the Data Protection Authority, told Dawan Media that the agency had begun registering data controllers and data processors as part of efforts to strengthen oversight of personal data management.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
